title: U.S. House · California's 10th Congressional District
area: East Bay, centered on Contra Costa County, including Concord, Martinez, Pittsburg, and Antioch.

context.text: This district's boundaries changed under California Proposition 50, the mid-decade congressional redistricting measure voters approved in November 2025. Incumbent Mark DeSaulnier and Republican Jeff Frese advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, defeating Katherine Piccinini, Angela Griffiths, Josh Hamilton, Mitchell Maisler, and Bob Rowland.

candidates.name: Mark DeSaulnier
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with about 60% of the vote.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for California's 10th Congressional District (since 2023; previously the 11th District, 2015-2023)

summary.text: Mark DeSaulnier is the Democratic incumbent representing California's 10th Congressional District, which covers much of Contra Costa County and part of Alameda County. A former Bay Area restaurant owner, he served on the Contra Costa County Board of Supervisors, as mayor of Concord, and in the California Assembly and Senate before his election to Congress in 2014. He sits on the Education and Workforce and Transportation and Infrastructure committees and is Ranking Member of the House Ethics Committee; he is running for re-election.

background.text: Born in Lowell, Massachusetts. Earned a high school diploma from Cranwell Preparatory School and a B.A. in history from the College of the Holy Cross in 1974; his first job, per his Ballotpedia survey, was as a deputy probation officer at Boston Juvenile Court during college.

According to his official biography, he moved to California in the early 1970s and over the next 35 years owned and managed several Bay Area restaurants, including Henry Africa's in San Francisco, Santa Fe Bar and Grill in Berkeley, and TR's in Concord. He was a member of the Teamsters and the Hotel Employees and Restaurant Employees unions.

Held local office as a member of the Contra Costa County Board of Supervisors and as mayor of Concord, and served on the California Air Resources Board (1997-2006), according to his campaign website, as well as the Bay Area Air Quality Management District and the Metropolitan Transportation Commission.

Served in the California State Assembly (District 11, 2006-2008) and the California State Senate (District 7, 2008-2014). His official biography says he was the first freshman in history to chair the Assembly Transportation Committee and later chaired the Senate Transportation and Housing Committee.
First elected to the U.S. House in 2014, taking office in January 2015, after advancing from the June 2014 primary and winning the general election in what was then the 11th District.

Sits on the Education and Workforce Committee, where he is Ranking Member of the Health, Employment, Labor, and Pensions Subcommittee, and on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee. Appointed to the House Ethics Committee in the 118th Congress, where he is now Ranking Member; previously served on the Rules Committee, where he was Vice Chair.

His office says he has passed more than 60 legislative efforts in Congress and that 61 of his bills became California law during his time in the state legislature. His office received a Congressional Management Foundation Democracy Award in 2019.
Lives in Concord, where he raised his two sons, according to his official biography; he has also run 23 marathons.

priorities.text: Says he is focused on the cost of living, housing, and transportation in the Bay Area, citing his record securing funding for affordable housing and transportation projects in Contra Costa County.
Says he created the Future of Work, Wages, and Labor initiative on preparing workers for an AI economy, and wrote a CEO-pay tax bill adopted in Portland, Oregon.
Says he is a strong advocate for NIH funding and medical research, citing his own 2015 diagnosis with chronic lymphocytic leukemia.

positions.summary: Campaign site says he is fighting to protect California's vehicle emission standards and clean energy investments against federal rollbacks, citing his authorship of the Clean Corridors Act, a $2.5 billion national EV charging program.
Says he is a strong advocate for NIH funding in the appropriations process and is fighting against cuts to medical research funding.

Says he is advancing transit-oriented housing through the Equitable Transit Oriented Development Support Act and created a permanent state funding source for affordable housing as a state senator (SB 1220).

record.text: Serves as Ranking Member of the House Health, Employment, Labor, and Pensions Subcommittee and is the top Democrat on the House Committee on Ethics.
Assigned to the House Committee on Ethics and the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Authored the Clean Corridors Act, a $2.5 billion national EV charging program enacted in the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, and the Justice for Dislocated Workers Act.

candidates.name: Jeff Frese
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with about 13% of the vote.

summary.text: Jeff Frese is a small-business owner from Moraga, California, and the Republican nominee for California's 10th Congressional District. According to his Ballotpedia survey, he founded a snack company and sold it, now runs a skincare company, and earlier worked in product leadership at media companies. His campaign focuses on congressional term limits, affordability, and public safety.

background.text: Lives in Moraga, California. In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey he describes himself as a husband, a father of three daughters, and a coach.
Earned a bachelor's degree in economics from the State University of New York, Cortland, according to his Ballotpedia survey.
Says he worked in product leadership at CNN, Nickelodeon, and MTV before entering business ownership.

Says he founded the snack company Fat Snax in his kitchen, grew it into a national brand with nationwide distribution, and sold it; he says he now runs a skincare company. His first job, he says, was at age eight selling wild plants door to door.
He is the Republican nominee for the 10th District in 2026; he says the campaign takes no special-interest money and has no consultants or staff. He advanced from the June 2, 2026 primary.

priorities.text: Calls for 8-year term limits for members of Congress, a ban on members trading stocks, a "no budget, no pay" rule, and closing the "revolving door" to lobbying.
Says Congress's deficit spending drives up mortgage rates and housing prices, and calls for cutting red tape on home building and banning Wall Street firms from buying single-family homes.
Calls for backing police, ending cashless bail, and getting fentanyl off the streets with what he calls real consequences for dealers.

positions.summary: Campaign site calls for backing the police, prosecuting crime, ending cashless bail, and keeping repeat offenders off the streets.
Campaign site calls for cutting red tape that makes building homes slow and expensive.
